title: D-Wave Delivers Italy's First Annealing Quantum Computer to Lombardy Infrastructure Hub
excerpt: D-Wave has installed Italy's first on-premises Advantage2 annealing quantum computer at Villa Saporiti in Como. Funded by Swiss Quantum Technology SA (SQT) with a €10 million agreement, this 4,400+ qubit system will be accessible to European researchers and businesses both on-site and remotely via D-Wave's Leap cloud service. This initiative supports the Volta Declaration's goals for quantum computing and AI development in Europe, coinciding with the bicentennial of Alessandro Volta's death.
content:
Dual-platform quantum hardware and software provider D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) has delivered an Advantage2 annealing quantum computer to Villa Saporiti in Como, Italy, marking the installation of the country’s first on-premises annealing quantum system.

Funded through a €10 million agreement with Swiss Quantum Technology SA (SQT), the 4,400+ qubit system, designated internally as the VoltaB1 within the Q-Alliance ecosystem, provides European research universities and commercial enterprises with direct physical access to production-grade quantum annealing hardware. Under the commercial agreement, SQT acquired 50% of the system’s operational capacity for five years, holding an option to purchase full ownership of the installation. Once fully configured, the system will be accessible remotely via D-Wave’s Leap cloud service.

The system’s arrival at Villa Saporiti forms part of the lead-up to the bicentennial of Alessandro Volta’s death and follows the signing of the Volta Declaration at the World Tech Conference in Milan, establishing a collaborative framework for quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and sovereign European digital infrastructure.
